title: What If They Ate The Baby? by @Xhloe and Natasha at Soho Playhouse #w...
transcript: Two high-strung, McCarthy-era housewives find themselves in a recurring fever dream — and what is that bumping sound upstairs? This describes the latest offering from fringe hitmakers Xhloe and Natasha, and it's fantastic. If you've never seen their work before, they combine this distinctive physicality and meticulously choreographed delivery with absurdism and clowning. Watching them perform together is like witnessing a magic trick — they're always perfectly aligned, almost moving as one theatrical organism. This piece is funny, sad, and unsettling. It starts with Dottie showing up at Shirley's house to return a casserole dish, but this seemingly everyday interaction ends up going much deeper. As the piece unfolds, their walls unravel and more layers of their relationship surface. Part of the genius of this piece is how its repetitive structure is used to reflect the world and the mindsets of these characters, while bringing new ideas into the picture. A simple question like “do you trust me?” takes on a completely new meaning by the end of the play, and the subtext that you can cut with a knife in the opening scene hesitantly transforms into something much more pointed by the end. What If They Ate The Baby? is running at Soho Playhouse through December 22nd, and it's not to be missed. With that, another program for my collection.
